- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 73+), overshooting by 2–5% in subsequent periods; apply dampening factor of 0.95–0.98 to peak forecasts.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 73→65→62), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias correction for 3–5 periods after peak.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 72+ → 70+); apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
